newsitem.title: FRANCE: Santer, Bruton urge budget discipline.
newsitem.headline: Santer, Bruton urge budget discipline.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer and Irish Prime Minister John Bruton both called on Wednesday for continued strict budgetary discipline to make the single European currency a reality.

"Stable public finances deliver low interest rates, low inflation, higher investment and ultimately more jobs," Bruton, whose country is current European Union president, told the European Parliament.
He said economic and monetary union (EMU) must begin on time and that it would cement the intergration of Europe's people.
Santer warned against listening to opponents of monetary union.
"Work must be continued. It must not be weakened by false arguments that budetary rigour will bring on recession and unemployment," he told Euro-MPs.
Citing the Netherlands, Denmark and Ireland, Santer noted that a number of states that had worked hard to cut deficits had also seen good results in their employment figures.
"The single currency will come. It will come on January 1, 1999. A substantial number of countries will be in at the start," he said.
